text: This is tripwire, a stop-loss for your Mon: if the price falls, a bot sells it for you, and only on your terms.
cap: tripwire is a stop-loss for your MON: if the price falls, a bot sells it for you, and only on your terms.

text: I'm Dan. I hold Mon, a crypto coin. What if the bot selling it for me gets hacked?
cap: I'm Dan. I hold MON, a crypto coin. What if the bot selling it for me gets hacked?

text: Other stop-loss bots can sell however they like once you grant them. With tripwire, the chain refuses any sale I did not sign.

text: This is live on the real Monad network, with real money, kept small.

text: First, my plan. A stop sells when the price falls to a line I pick. The price is the average over the last sixty seconds, so one spike cannot trip it.
cap: A stop sells when the price falls to a line I pick. The price is the average over the last 60 seconds, so one spike cannot trip it.

text: Row one sells zero point three Mon. I set its line above today's price, only so you can watch it sell. A real stop sits below.

text: Every row has a floor, the lowest price it may sell at. Row two, zero point two Mon, sits ten percent below, so it should never sell.

text: Now a wallet. A pass key is the wallet. It opens with my fingerprint, with no extension and no seed phrase.

text: I put one Mon into it.

text: One pass key prompt signs the plan, and the signed plan goes to Monad.

text: Now the keeper, the bot that sells for me, is watching. Row one's line is already crossed.

text: It sells exactly zero point three Mon, once, and the money lands in my own wallet.

text: Read straight from the chain: the money from the sale is there, and row two is still unsold.

text: Now the bad day: the keeper is hacked. This button makes the real keeper try a forbidden sale.

text: First, it sells before the price reaches my line.
